citation: Slaby, Jan, and Gerhard Thonhauser. "Heidegger and the Affective (Un)Grounding of Politics." In Heidegger on Affect, edited by Christos Hadjioannou, 265-290. Philosophers in Depth. Cham: Palgrave Macmillan, 2019. Chapter 12 of 12 (final chapter). Hadjioannou is the volume's editor only; the chapter is co-authored by Slaby and Thonhauser.
thesis: Heidegger's account of Grundstimmungen (basic attunements) -- angst in Being and Time, boredom in The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics -- discloses the radical ungroundedness and contingency of human existence, and this disclosure constitutes the founding, ontological dimension of 'the political' as distinct from ordinary institutional 'politics.' This same affective disclosure of ungroundedness does not itself dictate any particular political response: it can be answered democratically (per Arendt and Lefort) or, as in Heidegger's own 1933/34 Rektoratszeit collaboration with the NSDAP, autocratically. An 'inevitable ambivalence' therefore inhabits any ontology of political affectivity that discloses contingency without determining how that contingency ought to be lived.

sections.title: [Introduction, unlabeled]
sections.summary: States the political-ontological thesis distinguishing 'the political' (ontological ungrounding-ground) from 'politics' (ontic sub-system); previews the chapter roadmap; invokes Lefort's 'radically democratic situation' and Arendt's dictum that freedom is the raison d'etre of politics; flags Heidegger's 1933 Nazi turn as the chapter's cautionary case.

sections.title: 2. The Gist of Befindlichkeit
sections.summary: Reconstructs Heidegger's general theory of mood/attunement from FCM Section 17 and Being and Time Sections 29-30: findingness (Befindlichkeit) as the passive-receptive dimension of being-in-the-world, disclosing facticity and thrownness (Geworfenheit); findingness is constitutively prone to falling (Verfallen), which is why angst and boredom mostly remain latent behind everyday distraction.

sections.title: 3. Angst--Breakdown of Significance
sections.summary: Reconstructs BT Section 40's phenomenology of angst via the fear/angst contrast (fear is directed at a particular threatening entity; angst is objectless, disclosing 'nothing and nowhere'); develops a two-plane model of existence (ungrounded depth vs. stabilized everyday surface) and reads this model as directly analogous to the relation between ordinary politics and 'the political' as such; closes by glossing angst's disclosure of freedom in Arendtian terms.

sections.title: 4. Profound Boredom
sections.summary: Reconstructs FCM's tripartite typology of boredom (becoming-bored-by, being-bored-with, profound boredom), concentrating on the second and third forms via the dinner-party and 'undifferentiated no one' material; argues that Heidegger, unlike in the angst analysis, explicitly frames boredom's Grundstimmung as an attunement of a Volk (people) rather than an individual dasein, and that this communal reframing licenses Heidegger's demand for a collective, activist self-determination.

sections.title: 5. The Collapse of Dasein and Work in the Rektoratszeit
sections.summary: Via Werner Hamacher's critique of Heidegger's 'Rektorats-Philosophie,' traces how 'work' (Arbeit) occupies, in the 1933 'Rede an Arbeitslose' and a 1934 Logic Lecture (GA 38:128), the structural place BT and FCM reserve for the Augenblick; notes postwar German continuity in prizing Arbeit and Heidegger's later reversal on work (via his Ernst Junger/Der Arbeiter notes). Footnote 5 states this section is 'reproduced with permission from Slaby (2017b)' -- i.e., from bor-sec-12, whose own 'Interlude' section covers identical ground.

sections.title: 6. The Affective (Un)Grounding of Politics
sections.summary: Synthesis, sharing its title with the chapter: recaps angst's and boredom's shared disclosure of ungroundedness; develops Lefort's 'empty place of power' and 'People-as-One' as the poles of a democracy/totalitarianism antagonism; surveys republican (Arendt, Lefort) and agonistic (Ranciere, Mouffe) postfoundational responses without adjudicating between them; concludes the same antagonism is latent within Heidegger's own itinerary -- his texts stage the sharpest postfoundational insight available, while Heidegger the political actor answered it autocratically.

sections.title: Notes
sections.summary: Eight endnotes: funding acknowledgments (DFG CRC 1171 Affective Societies; FWF J-4055-G24) and thanks to readers including Andreas Elpidorou, Dermot Moran, and Erik Ringmar; BT citation conventions; a further-reading list on Befindlichkeit (Elpidorou and Freeman 2015 x2, Ratcliffe 2013, Slaby 2015/2017a, Withy 2014/2015); the Augenblick/Kierkegaard note; the Slaby (2017b) attribution for Section 5; an Aristotelian-vs-Platonic gloss on Arendt's and Heidegger's respective views of politics (cf. Theodorou 2013).

sections.summary: Full reference list including Agamben, Arendt, Butler, Elpidorou and Freeman (2015 x2), Hamacher, Haugeland, Hoerl, Kantorowicz, Lacoue-Labarthe and Nancy, Lefort (1986, 1988), Marchart, Mouffe,Ranciere, Ratcliffe, Ringmar, Slaby (2015, 2017a, 2017b), Theodorou, and Withy (2012, 2014, 2015).

constructs.label: profound/deep boredom (FCM 3rd form)
constructs.treatment: undifferentiated no one, indifference of entities as a whole, telling-refusal-as-telling, Augenblick; distinctively read as a Volk-attunement (communal) rather than an individual psychological state

constructs.label: being-bored-with (2nd form)
constructs.treatment: dinner-party example retold compactly; self abandoned in an 'odd suspension'; standing now (stehendes Jetzt) as existential futility

constructs.label: being-bored-by (1st form)
constructs.treatment: named only via the train-station example; not developed, mirroring bor-sec-12's identical bracketing

constructs.label: temporality of boredom (time-drag)
constructs.treatment: Langeweile as lived-time-becoming-long, glossed via Bergson's duree; standing now; fused threefold temporal horizon of profound boredom

constructs.label: monotony / meaninglessness
constructs.treatment: breakdown of everyday significance in angst (SZ 186); indifference of entities as a whole in profound boredom (FCM 138/GA 208)

constructs.label: boredom-as-regulatory-signal (functional account)
constructs.treatment: telling-refusal-as-telling reconstructed faithfully, then politicized: the signal's addressee is a Volk, and its demand is collective self-founding rather than individual authenticity

constructs.label: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
constructs.treatment: dinner-party's outward lively participation masking underlying boredom (surface/depth divergence)

constructs.label: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
constructs.treatment: diffuse; findingness's 'evasive turning away' (SZ 136) as Heidegger's general theory of falling, not an empirical claim about attention (P/anticipatory-application for any cognitive-science mapping)

constructs.label: situational vs. trait/state boredom; boredom proneness; mind-wandering/task-unrelated thought
constructs.treatment: not addressed in the psychological idiom; actively contested rather than merely absent, since Heidegger explicitly denies Grundstimmung can be verified via individual introspection (FCM 60/GA 90f)

readings.claim: Angst is objectless and thus potentially limitless in scope; what oppresses in angst is 'nothing and nowhere,' a collapse of everyday significance disclosing a baseline ungroundedness of all and everything.

Existence has two intertwined, unstable planes -- an ungrounded depth and a stabilizing everyday surface -- and this structure is directly analogous to the relation between ordinary institutional politics and 'the political' as such.

Angst individualizes dasein yet simultaneously discloses dasein's own active role in constituting a meaningful world, which is, in Arendtian terms, the essence of the political: freedom as plural self-determination under conditions of indeterminacy.

Unlike angst, profound boredom's Grundstimmung is explicitly framed by Heidegger as an attunement of a Volk rather than an individual dasein -- 'our' attunement, not 'the' attunement of any single person.
readings.stance: restates-FCM (fcm-06/fcm-07), novel emphasis relative to bor-sec-12/13

readings.claim: The demand profound boredom's 'telling refusal' places on 'us' is transformed by Heidegger into a mobilizing appeal, a call to arms addressed to a political community rather than to a private self.
From roughly Section 38 of the FCM lecture onward, the text's register shifts from existential ontology toward rhetoric the authors read as anticipating Heidegger's Rektoratszeit politics.

In the 1933 'Rede an Arbeitslose' and a 1934 Logic Lecture, Heidegger installs Arbeit (work) at exactly the structural place -- the Augenblick -- that BT and FCM reserve for resolute, authentic temporality.

The postwar prizing of work did not end with denazification, and Heidegger himself later reversed course, coming to see work as the metaphysical epitome of modern subjectivity rather than existential salvation.

Heidegger's analyses of angst and boredom are among the most acute available expositions of postfoundational political affectivity, yet Heidegger himself could not bear the openness his own analyses disclosed, responding with a demand for decisive authority that forecloses rather than sustains democratic contestation.

Following Lefort, democracy is defined by power occupying an 'empty place' no group can permanently claim, while totalitarianism reunifies society around a single 'People-as-One'; this same antagonism is latently operative within Heidegger's own itinerary, his 1933/34 turn serving as a case in point of the totalitarian resolution.

The chapter surveys, without adjudicating, a republican/consensual postfoundational lineage (Arendt, Lefort) and an agonistic/conflictual one (Ranciere's 'part of those without part'; Mouffe's arena of substantive conflict).
An 'inevitable ambivalence' inhabits any ontology of political affectivity that discloses ungroundedness without thereby determining how that ungroundedness is to be answered.

tensions.axis: angst as individualizing disclosure (BT) vs. boredom as communalizing, Volk-directed disclosure (FCM)
tensions.note: The chapter's own most consequential textual observation, not present in bor-sec-12 or bor-sec-13: Heidegger's two Grundstimmungen are read as diverging on whether the attuned 'subject' is an individual dasein or a historical people.

tensions.axis: ontological disclosure of ungroundedness/freedom vs. Heidegger's own autocratic political response to that disclosure
tensions.note: The chapter's central critical claim: the phenomenology does not determine the politics; Heidegger's actual 1933/34 choice is presented as one possible (and disastrous) response among others.

tensions.axis: republican/consensual postfoundationalism (Arendt, Lefort) vs. agonistic/conflictual postfoundationalism (Rancière, Mouffe)
tensions.note: Surveyed side by side in Section 6 without the authors adjudicating which line best follows from the Heideggerian premises they reconstruct.

tensions.axis: boredom's regulatory 'message' read as demanding individual authenticity (bor-sec-12/13's register) vs. read as demanding collective, Volk-level self-founding (this chapter's register)
tensions.note: Same FCM textual base, different addressee of the demand -- a genuine interpretive divergence across Slaby's own oeuvre, most visible when this unit is set beside bor-sec-12/13.
